page: Microsoft Azure F64-16amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per core. Additionally, it includes 7559 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are present.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations placing in the top 10%. Multi-threaded performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores falling in the average range. Memory performance is strong, with a Passmark memory score in the top 25% and cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 3201.99 GB/sec. For lightweight AI workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds of 420.88 tokens/second for small LLM models.

Given its massive 512 GB memory capacity and 7.5 TB of local NVMe SSD storage relative to its 16 vCPUs, this server offers high resource density. It is highly cost-efficient for memory-bound and storage-heavy workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. The hardware profile is well-suited for large in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
